subject: MAP & evaluation checkpoints — commitments, discounts, and SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Samir Kahn <samir.kahn@datasight.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — proposed deliverables and timeline

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the draft MAP and the eval checklist. Couple quick items from our side before we lock dates:

- Evaluation scope: we want to validate latency at production-ish QPS (target 100 TPS) and an end-to-end median/95th pctl on our test corpus. Can you confirm the load harness you plan to use?
- SLA asks: we typically require an availability SLA and SLOs for 95th-pctl latency. If Redwood is requesting commit/discounts we need clarity on service credits for missed latency SLOs.
- Ramp: we’d be comfortable with a 30-day pilot at 10% of production, moving to 50% after acceptance.

I attached a short internal checklist. If you can make the SLO/credit schedule explicit in the MAP, we can route legal. Goal for us is a hard close by end of Feb.

— Samir
Head of ML Engineering, DataSight
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Samir Kahn <samir.kahn@datasight.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — proposed deliverables and timeline

Samir — great notes, thanks. Short answers up front:

- Load harness: we’ll use our k6-based harness (shared Drive link in attachments) configured to mimic 100 TPS sustained with variable token-length distributions. We can run in your VPC for the pilot or through our hosted staging environment — your preference.
- Latency SLOs: proposal below (open to adjustments):
  * Median latency: <= 60ms token-gen for baseline prompt set
  * 95th percentile: <= 220ms for single-stream inference at target QPS
  * Availability: 99.9% monthly
- Credits: if 95th pctl exceeds agreed threshold in a rolling 7-day window, we propose service credits starting at 5% of monthly committed fee for first breach, 10% for second within 30 days.

I’ve attached an updated MAP (v1b) with milestone dates tied to evaluation checkpoints and commercial triggers (commits and discounts). Suggested ramp and discounting logic:
  * Commit tier A: $50k/month — baseline pricing, 5% committed discount after 3 months ramp-in
  * Commit tier B: $150k/month — 10% committed discount, includes burst capacity
  * Early-close credit: sign by 2026-02-28 and we’ll provide $10k in platform credits applied against month 1

If you’re ok, I’ll run this by Marissa for approval on commercial concessions and loop in Vivek to validate the SLO technical feasibility.

Thanks — Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal — DataSight MAP: SLO/credit ask + ramp/discount plan

Team — forwarding Samir’s asks and my proposed counters (see attached DataSight_MAP_v1b.pdf). Need quick alignment on two fronts before I send final to the customer:

1) SLO feasibility (Vivek): can our hosted/Dedicated variants meet a 95th pctl <= 220ms under 100 TPS for the targeted prompt set? If not, what realistic pctl can we guarantee for the pilot vs GA? Also confirm what monitoring traces we can expose for their SREs.

2) Commercial approvals (Marissa + Monica): I proposed a credit schedule (5% / 10% escalating) and an early-close $10k platform credit. We need sign-off to include credits in the MAP. This is a sales-motion concession tied directly to committing to tier A or B.

Notes: Legal will want explicit definitions (measurement window, SLA windows, exclusions) — mark these as TBD in the MAP until legal weighs in.

— Rishi

> 2) Credit calculation: we prefer credits tied to monthly committed spend rather than the total platform invoice if that simplifies calculations (i.e., credits against the committed tier fee).

Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation checkpoints — commitments, discounts, and SLA tradeoffs

Samir — appreciate the concrete asks. We updated the MAP to include: 

- Read-only dashboard access for the pilot (links + dashboard view permissions will be provided once the pilot environment is provisioned).
- Credit calculation: service credits will be applied against the monthly committed tier fee (per your request).
- Ramp-triggered discounts: explicit clause — when average routed production volume to Redwood reaches >=50% of target for 10 consecutive days within the first 60 days, the commit discount moves from 5% to 10% (applies to next billing cycle).

Attached: DataSight_MAP_v1b.pdf (redlines) and eval_plan_q1.xlsx.

Next steps / timeline:
- 2026-02-20: finalize MAP and commercial terms (this email thread)
- 2026-02-22: legal to issue MSA/DocuSign
- 2026-02-24: provisioning and pilot start (10% traffic)
- 2026-03-25: acceptance and ramp to 50% (subject to eval pass)

If this matches your ask I’ll instruct legal to prepare the DocuSign (HubSpot link included). We can target close by 2026-02-28 if legal moves quickly.

Best — Rishi
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Internal — DataSight MAP: SLO/credit ask + ramp/discount plan

Quick technical confirmation for the record (looping relevant parts of the thread):

- Feasibility: Dedicated pool (A100x2 nodes) with our optimized kernels and KV cache settings can meet 95th pctl <= 220ms at 100 TPS for the provided prompt set. We’ll need to validate token-length distributions during the first 48 hours of the pilot and reserve headroom for spikes.
- Observability: we can provide a read-only Grafana dashboard (95/99/median pctl, request IDs, error rates) and a link to a raw CSV export for their SRE team.
- Exclusions: maintenance windows and customer misconfiguration (e.g., sending batched requests beyond agreed QPS) will be excluded from credit calculations — we’ll enumerate exclusions in the SLO appendix.

I’ll prepare a short tech appendix to attach to the MAP that defines measurement window (rolling 7-day), test harness config, and examples for the credit calc.

— Vivek
Senior Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
